experiment: SLA / throughput load test (#5) — on-device Raspberry Pi 5 (aarch64 A76)
headline: 50,000 sustained adversarial (Logarithmic-phase) queries at back-to-back max rate: 0 SLA violations at the corrected 50 ms budget. p99 latency 0.0021 ms is ~24,000x under the 50 ms SLA. Per-thread compute CPU saturates (peak 99.8%) at max offered rate.

data.batch: 200 real UNSW-NB15 d=42 adversarial samples, LOAD_SCALE=5 to push into Logarithmic (adversarial) phase

throughput.why: wall_s (0.181 s) includes ~0.10 s fixed thread-spawn/join overhead; pure compute path is 50000 x 1.57 us ~= 0.078 s, so true sustained processing rate is higher than the reported qps. Reported qps is a conservative lower bound.

honest_findings.SLA_headroom: The 50 ms Edge SLA is trivially satisfied; even at back-to-back offered (max-load) adversarial traffic, zero inferences exceed budget. Not a binding constraint.
honest_findings.cpu: The single compute/driver thread reaches ~100% of its core at max offered rate, confirming the pipeline is CPU-bound only at artificially-maximal (back-to-back) offered load.
honest_findings.per_query_cost_scope: This per-query latency (p50 0.0014 ms) covers the COMPUTE path only (defense->budget-gated rotation->TFLite inference), not the full 3-thread channel orchestration of the deployed pipeline (which #6 measured end-to-end at ~0.10 ms). Both are far inside 50 ms.
honest_findings.phase_independence: Throughput is phase-independent: the Artificial/Logarithmic phase changes only scalar rotation math with identical cost, so adversarial-phase load does not alter the SLA/latency conclusion.
